our_argument_summary: WIN-057b argues that the dome-claimed "Global Cavity Re-Pressurization" — inferred from synchronous magnetic decay at three INTERMAGNET stations (labeled TTB/VSS/HER) — is standard MHD geophysics relabeled. Terra-Nova et al. (2017) derive SAA splitting from CMB reversed-flux patches; multi-station correlation is expected because all three stations sit within the SAA spatial correlation length. The dome has no mechanism for "cavity rupture" and the claim substantially duplicates evidence already counted in WIN-004/005/035/041. Verdict: Std Model Explains.

holes_found.description: Our review text labels "TTB (Namibia)" — but per the authoritative INTERMAGNET GIN capabilities registry (fetched 2026-07-21 from imag-data.bgs.ac.uk), IAGA code TTB = Tatuoca, Brazil (-1.205°, -48.513°E). The station at (-19.202°, 17.584°E) in Namibia is actually IAGA code TSU (Tsumeb). Either (a) the dome text mislabels the station code and our review passed the error through unchallenged, or (b) our review mislabeled the station on its own. c1 quantitative_verification computed distances using TSU coordinates (-19.2°, 17.6°) and labeled them TTB, producing a self-consistent but factually wrong table. If TTB really is Tatuoca, Brazil, then TTB-VSS distance is ~2,414 km (both in Brazil), TTB-HER is ~7,900 km, HER-VSS 6,199 km — different geometry from what c1 tabulated. The "same anomaly, correlated within 5,000-8,000 km" argument still holds (max pair ~7,900 km sits at the upper edge), but the specific numbers and station identification need fixing.
holes_found.recommendation: Two-step. (1) Verify the current dome site text for WIN-057b — does the dome say "TTB (Namibia)" or "TSU (Namibia)" or "TTB (Brazil)"? Whichever it is, cite it accurately. (2) If the dome mislabeled the station code, our review should explicitly note the code error ("the dome cites IAGA code TTB but the coordinates given are TSU, Tsumeb, Namibia") — that is itself an argument against the dome's claimed rigor. If the dome correctly says TSU, our review should switch to TSU. Then re-run the quantitative_verification with correct station coordinates. IAGA TTB coords: -1.205°N, -48.513°W. IAGA TSU coords: -19.202°N, 17.584°E.

holes_found.description: The Alken et al. 2021 citation (DOI 10.1186/s40623-021-01569-z) — added by patch after c1 flagged the original 10.1029/2020GL087323 as broken — resolves via CrossRef to "Special issue 'International Geomagnetic Reference Field: the thirteenth generation'" published in Earth, Planets and Space (2022, per CrossRef issued date). This is a special-issue EDITORIAL, not the substantive IGRF-13 model paper. The substantive paper — which actually documents SAA structure at IGRF-13 vintage — is Alken et al. 2021, DOI 10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x, "International Geomagnetic Reference Field: the thirteenth generation" (verified via CrossRef 2026-07-21, Earth Planets and Space, authors P. Alken, E. Thébault, C. Beggan, H. Amit, J. Aubert). The editorial does not carry the SAA-second-minimum-emerging-near-20°S,10°E evidence at the depth our claim needs.
holes_found.recommendation: Swap the DOI in detail_evidence from 10.1186/s40623-021-01569-z to 10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x. Keep the citation year as 2021. The URL pattern is the same (Earth Planets Space, https://doi.org/10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x). This is a citation-target precision fix, not a claim change.

stronger_arguments.description: The c1 review's station-identification argument (TTB and HER both in southern Africa relative to VSS in Brazil) is undermined by the TTB=Brazil discovery above — but a stronger argument is now available. If IAGA TTB (Tatuoca, Brazil, -1.2°S) is genuinely one of the three stations the dome cites, then TTB sits at ONLY 1.2° south of the equator and VSS at 22.4°S — the two Brazilian stations span 21° of latitude across the SAA's spatial extent, which if anything strengthens "same anomaly, correlated coverage" because you are sampling the SAA at its northern edge (TTB) AND its center (VSS). The dome's claim that this is a "structural rupture" would need to explain why the rupture happens to align with the SAA's known spatial footprint at both stations.
sources: Terra-Nova et al. 2017 for SAA spatial extent modeling

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's claim of "global" cavity re-pressurization remains vulnerable to the Northern Hemisphere silence argument c1 raised — no Northern-Hemisphere INTERMAGNET stations (Niemegk, Chambon-la-Forêt, Boulder) are invoked as showing synchronous acceleration. If the cause were a global structural change at r ≈ 20,000 km, effects should distribute across both hemispheres. The absence of Northern claims is preserved in our review's omission but not made explicit — surfacing it in the detail_evidence prose would strengthen the argument.

kernel_of_truth.description: The SAA genuinely has bifurcated into two intensity minima with the coordinates the dome cites (roughly 26.6°S, 49.1°W and 20.0°S, 10.0°E), and stations across the affected region do show correlated secular variation — these are real observations from a real monitoring network (Terra-Nova et al. 2017 [monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/WIN-057b.c2.json:citation_check]). The dome author correctly identifies the dual-lobe structure and its ongoing evolution.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Accurately reporting an observation is not the same as predicting it. The dome (data/wins.json:057b) offers no equations linking disc_radius, firmament_height, or any dome geometric parameter to the observed lobe coordinates or decay rates. MHD models (Terra-Nova 2017, DOI 10.1016/j.pepi.2017.03.002) derive both the lobe positions and the multi-station correlation from first principles; the dome contribution is a narrative label ("Ovoid Shoulder shift at r ≈ 20,000 km"), and the numerical match between "r ≈ 20,000 km" and disc_radius=20,015 km is a naming coincidence rather than a derivation.

deeper_analysis: Two substantive findings this cycle. First and most important: the TTB-vs-TSU station-code confusion. Per the authoritative INTERMAGNET GIN capabilities XML (imag-data.bgs.ac.uk, fetched 2026-07-21), IAGA code TTB = Tatuoca, Brazil (-1.2°S, -48.5°W); the Namibia station at (-19.2°S, 17.6°E) is IAGA code TSU (Tsumeb). Our review says "TTB (Namibia)" which is factually wrong on the code-country pairing. c1 quantitative_verification produced internally-consistent numbers using TSU coordinates while labeling them TTB — the c1 numbers are correct for the point (-19.2°, 17.6°) but the point is not TTB. This needs a two-step fix: (a) verify what the dome site actually says today, and (b) either correct our review's label OR call out the dome's code error explicitly. Either way, quantitative_verification should be re-run once identification is settled. Second: the Alken 2021 replacement DOI recommended by c1 landed on the special-issue editorial (10.1186/s40623-021-01569-z) instead of the primary IGRF-13 model paper (10.1186/s40623-020-01288-x). The citation resolves but the specific target does not carry the SAA-second-minimum evidence our claim needs. A one-line DOI swap fixes this. Positive: the c1 critical finding (broken DOI 10.1029/2020GL087323) HAS been resolved — the current text no longer contains that DOI. c1 minor #3 (detail_group precision) is a persistent low-priority organizational nit and is unchanged. The core Std Model Explains verdict is not in question; both new findings are precision/citation issues, not verdict challenges.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A fair-minded dome defender could reply: "You caught our station-code confusion — thank you for the correction — but the substantive claim is unchanged. Whether the three stations are TTB(Brazil)+VSS(Brazil)+HER(SA) or TSU(Namibia)+VSS(Brazil)+HER(SA), they still span roughly the SAA region and still show correlated decay. Your review's own kernel_of_truth grants that the correlated decay is a real observation. Fixing our station code is trivial. The deeper question — whether 'MHD explains this from first principles' or 'the dome relabels a real observation' — is unchanged by the code fix. And your Alken editorial citation just proved the same failure mode you accuse us of: citing an authoritative-sounding source that does not carry the specific evidence your claim needs. Fix your own citation before demanding we fix ours."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Fold the station-code issue into the review as a positive example ("here is a nit we found via a five-minute registry lookup that the dome has apparently missed for months"). Fix the Alken DOI first — a broken-target citation being caught in adversarial review is fine; leaving one in the published text is not. Once both fixes land, the "you cite as sloppily as we do" rebuttal disappears.
